tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
definition.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

query.description: Semantic lookup of tools for the data you need. Selectors constrain the search.

providers.description: Values from each listed tool's `provider` field (e.g. "apps-apple-com"). Alone, lists that provider's compact tools; with capabilities, scopes them.

categories.description: Category IDs returned by an empty call. Lists providers by default.

groups.description: Optional group IDs for explicit group browsing.

capabilities.description: Values from each listed tool's `capability` field (e.g. "apps/app"). Put the provider in `providers`: {"providers": ["apps-apple-com"], "capabilities": ["apps/app"]}. A selected capability expands its complete contract by default.

level.description: Usually omit: it follows the arguments (tools for query, urls, providers, capabilities or groups; providers for categories; categories with none). Set providers or groups to list those within a category or url scope instead of tools. query, or a non-empty expand with any other argument, returns tools.

expand.description: Use ["options", "response"] for inputs and output shape without example payloads; [] keeps results compact. Omit for full contracts on selected capabilities.

includeCosts.description: Include per-capability credit prices (creditsCost, perRecord) in tool results.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
definition.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

valuableResults.description: Every result that was actually useful, copied from the `source` and `position` stamped on each result. Each group is numbered from 1 independently, so the source is required — `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — unlisted results are treated as not useful. Do not also list the same results in valuableSources.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
definition.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

query.description: Semantic lookup of tools for the data you need. Selectors constrain the search.

providers.description: Values from each listed tool's `provider` field (e.g. "apps-apple-com"). Alone, lists that provider's compact tools; with capabilities, scopes them.

categories.description: Category IDs returned by an empty call. Lists providers by default.

groups.description: Optional group IDs for explicit group browsing.

capabilities.description: Values from each listed tool's `capability` field (e.g. "apps/app"). Put the provider in `providers`: {"providers": ["apps-apple-com"], "capabilities": ["apps/app"]}. A selected capability expands its complete contract by default.

level.description: Usually omit: it follows the arguments (tools for query, urls, providers, capabilities or groups; providers for categories; categories with none). Set providers or groups to list those within a category or url scope instead of tools. query, or a non-empty expand with any other argument, returns tools.

expand.description: Use ["options", "response"] for inputs and output shape without example payloads; [] keeps results compact. Omit for full contracts on selected capabilities.

includeCosts.description: Include per-capability credit prices (creditsCost, perRecord) in tool results.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
definition.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

valuableResults.description: Every result that was actually useful, copied from the `source` and `position` stamped on each result. Each group is numbered from 1 independently, so the source is required — `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — unlisted results are treated as not useful. Do not also list the same results in valuableSources.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

content.content:
156:- **Times** are Unix epoch **seconds** (e.g. `startTime`/`endTime` filters, activity `start_time`).
157-- **IDs** are UUID strings.
158-- **Live OpenAPI spec:** `GET /docs/spec` returns the full OAS JSON for the running API (authenticated) — useful for confirming exact schemas without the docs site.
159-- **Fair usage:** Catapult enforces fair-usage guidelines; abusive access can be revoked.
160-
161-### Data model (how entities relate)
162-
--
173:  "filters": [
174-    { "name": "activity_id", "comparison": "=", "values": ["<uuid>"] }
175-  ],
176-  "group_by": ["athlete", "activity"],
177-  "sorting": ["total_player_load"],
178-  "requested_only": true
179-}
--
184:- `filters`: ALL conditions must match. Comparisons: `=`, `<>`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`. Values are arrays of ids or epoch seconds (e.g. filter `date` / `start_time` ranges with `>=` + `<=` pairs).
185-- `group_by`: grouping by an entity adds its `id` and `name` to each row (`group_by: ["activity"]` → `activity_id`, `activity_name`).
186-- `requested_only: true` returns only the requested parameters (smaller payloads).
187-
188-## Troubleshooting & Gotchas
189-
190-| Symptom | Cause / Fix |
--
196:| `/stats` query hangs or fails | 60-second timeout on the endpoint for overly complex grouping combinations. Simplify `group_by`, narrow filters, split requests. No limit on number of activities otherwise. |
197-| Stats for activities AND periods needed | One call can't group both — make **separate calls** (FAQ-confirmed). |
198-| 10Hz sensor data empty/missing for an activity | Sensor files not synced to Cloud. Check `GET /activities?include=actdic_status` → `actdic_status.sd.munged` must show `synced > 0` and `unsynced: 0`. Data only exists in Cloud once the account owner uploads/syncs it. |

**Yes.** The API tracks PlayerLoad bands the same way it tracks heart rate bands.

**What I did**
- I installed the CLI. It is the newest build (2026.9.1), so it does not need an update. It is at `~/.local/bin/catapult-openfield-connect-pp-cli`. Your saved login works.
- I pulled the full metric list from the live API. It has 1,829 metrics, and 85 of them are PlayerLoad band metrics.
- I tested one real practice, UCF P3 on 10/27. All 88 athletes had numbers.

**What you can get for each band (1 to 8)**
- Time in the band: `player_load_band4_total_duration`, in seconds. This is the same idea as `hr_duration_band4`.
- Number of efforts in the band: `player_load_band4_total_effort_count`. Bands 2 to 8 only.
- Percent of the session spent in the band: `player_load_band4_duration_percentage`.

**"Time above band X"**
- No single metric gives this.
- To get it, add up the bands. For example, time above band 4 = band 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 durations.

**Band edges**
- One athlete's settings show: B1 0–1, B2 1–2, B3 2–3, B4 3–4, B5 4–6, B6 6+.
- These were set on 2020-02-06. They are probably the factory defaults.
- That athlete has no B7 or B8, but B7 and B8 still return data. So other athletes have different band settings.
- My guess is that the edges are PlayerLoad rate at each moment, not the session total. I did not confirm this.

**What I did not check**
- I did not confirm what unit the band edges use.
- The HR and velocity band 5 test columns came back as 0. I did not find out why.

**What you do now**
- Open OpenField → Settings → Bands → Player Load. Confirm the edges and the unit.
- If the edges were never tuned, set them before you trust the numbers.

I saved these facts in `~/DEV/Catapult_API/docs/STATUS.md` and pushed (commit `8913318`).

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Purpose

Athletic performance data infrastructure for Baylor University. The primary active project is an automated post-practice GPS report for Football using the Catapult API. ForceDecks integration is a separate, future project.

## Archived: `archive/coach_report/` (2026-10-19)

The post-session coach report (planned vs actual, max velocity, SPC flags) is **parked**: Eric is not moving forward with it. Code, tests, config and past reports (`archive/coach_report/Reports/coach/`) are kept as-is. `pull.sh` no longer builds it. To revive: move it back to `coach_report/` and restore the coach step in `gps_report/pull.sh` from git history (commit before 2026-10-19). Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-coach-report-design.md`.

## Active Project: `gps_report/`

**Automated post-practice GPS report** — pulls Football session data from Catapult Connect v6 API, stores summary stats in DuckDB, and generates a self-contained HTML report + plain-text email summary.

### Entry points
```
cd gps_report

# Daily report (after practice)
python run_report.py                          # interactive — picks today's session
python run_report.py --date 2026-03-10        # specific date
python run_report.py --session-id <uuid>      # skip picker
python run_report.py --list-positions         # print Catapult position strings (setup)
python run_report.py --force                  # re-import existing session

# Regular pull — the one command (also runs daily at 06:30 via launchd com.keystone.gpspull)
./pull.sh                                     # import new sessions (--since-db), then Parquet snapshots

# Bulk import
python bulk_import.py --since-db              # newest stored date − pull.overlap_days (3) → today
python bulk_import.py                         # 2025-03-22 → today (practices, walk-thrus, games, mock games)
python bulk_import.py --dry-run               # preview matching sessions without DB writes
python bulk_import.py --start 2025-08-01 --end 2025-12-31
python bulk_import.py --force                 # re-import sessions already in DB

# Tests (no network, no real DB)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q

# Backfill / recompute velocity + band columns for historical sessions
python backfill_velocity.py                   # all non-walk-through sessions
python backfill_velocity.py --dry-run         # preview without DB writes
python backfill_velocity.py --session-id <uuid>  # single session
```

### Session name conventions (Catapult)
| Type | Name pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Practice | standalone `P` token | `SP25 - P1 - 03.22.25`, `AUBURN - P3 - 08.26.25` |
| Walk-thru | contains `Walk Thru` | `SP25 - Walk Thru #1 - 03.24.25` |
| Game | standalone `G` token | `AUBURN - G1 - 08.29.25` |
| Mock game | contains `Mock Game` → day type `scrimmage` (kept out of practice norms and practice SPC history) | `FC26 - MOCK GAME - 08.29.26` |

### Install dependencies (first time only, macOS)
```
cd gps_report
~/.local/bin/uv venv .venv --python 3.14
~/.local/bin/uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-dev.txt
```
Never `pip install` globally (Python is PEP 668-managed on this Mac). `pull.sh` and launchd use `gps_report/.venv/bin/python`.

### Regular pull (added 2026-09-13)
- **Owner:** the Mac owns `data/gps_history.duckdb`. The Windows `Refresh_All_Data` GPS step must stay off (two writers = two drifting DBs).
- **Schedule:** `ops/com.keystone.gpspull.plist` → `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, daily 06:30; launchd runs a missed job on wake from sleep, not after power-off. Logs: `gps_report/logs/launchd-gpspull.{log,err}`.
- **Receipt:** every `bulk_import.py` run writes `logs/last_run.json` (status, exit code, window, counts, `imported_dates`, `last_success_at`). Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 usage/config/token · 2 DB open/lock · 3 partial · 4 all listing windows failed or roster fetch failed · 5 unexpected.
- **Alerts:** `pull.sh` appends one line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at Claude Code session start) on a non-zero import, a failed snapshot export, or no successful pull for 36 h.
- **Atomic sessions:** a session's header and athlete rows commit together or not at all; any stats row without an athlete id fails the session so it is retried.
- **Retry backlog:** the receipt's `retry_from` is the earliest date of any failed listing window or unstored session. The next `--since-db` run starts at the earlier of `newest − overlap_days` and `retry_from`, so a later success never strands an earlier failure. Only a clean `--since-db` run clears it; range and dry runs never do.
- Plan and Codex review: `docs/2026-09-13-pull-build-PLAN.md`, `docs/2026-09-13-pull-build-REVIEW-LOG.md`.

### Parquet snapshots for Windows (added 2026-09-24)
The DB never travels. After every ok/partial import, `pull.sh` runs `export_snapshot.py`, which opens the DB
read-only and writes one Parquet file per table to Google Drive. **Only the Mac writes them.** Windows reads
them directly and never writes the DB or the snapshots.
- **Where:** `$ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR/gps/`, else `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/gps/` on Drive
  (Mac `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/...`, Windows `G:\My Drive\...`).
  Files: `athlete_sessions.parquet`, `sessions.parquet`, `athletes.parquet`, `positional_norms.parquet`, plus
  `manifest.json` (per table: rows, bytes, written_at UTC, machine, newest `session_date`). No table is skipped
  (the DB has no log tables); `_`-prefixed work tables would be.

- Eric is not moving forward with the coach report. `coach_report/` moved to `archive/coach_report/` (history kept, past reports inside).
- `gps_report/pull.sh` no longer runs the coach step or its alerts. Import and Parquet snapshots are unchanged. Tests: 120 pass.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Purpose

Athletic performance data infrastructure for Baylor University. The primary active project is an automated post-practice GPS report for Football using the Catapult API. ForceDecks integration is a separate, future project.

## Archived: `archive/coach_report/` (2026-10-19)

The post-session coach report (planned vs actual, max velocity, SPC flags) is **parked**: Eric is not moving forward with it. Code, tests, config and past reports (`archive/coach_report/Reports/coach/`) are kept as-is. `pull.sh` no longer builds it. To revive: move it back to `coach_report/` and restore the coach step in `gps_report/pull.sh` from git history (commit before 2026-10-19). Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-coach-report-design.md`.

## Active Project: `gps_report/`

**Automated post-practice GPS report** — pulls Football session data from Catapult Connect v6 API, stores summary stats in DuckDB, and generates a self-contained HTML report + plain-text email summary.

### Entry points
```
cd gps_report

# Daily report (after practice)
python run_report.py                          # interactive — picks today's session
python run_report.py --date 2026-03-10        # specific date
python run_report.py --session-id <uuid>      # skip picker
python run_report.py --list-positions         # print Catapult position strings (setup)
python run_report.py --force                  # re-import existing session

# Regular pull — the one command (also runs daily at 06:30 via launchd com.keystone.gpspull)
./pull.sh                                     # import new sessions (--since-db), then Parquet snapshots

# Bulk import
python bulk_import.py --since-db              # newest stored date − pull.overlap_days (3) → today
python bulk_import.py                         # 2025-03-22 → today (practices, walk-thrus, games, mock games)
python bulk_import.py --dry-run               # preview matching sessions without DB writes
python bulk_import.py --start 2025-08-01 --end 2025-12-31
python bulk_import.py --force                 # re-import sessions already in DB

# Tests (no network, no real DB)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q

# Backfill / recompute velocity + band columns for historical sessions
python backfill_velocity.py                   # all non-walk-through sessions
python backfill_velocity.py --dry-run         # preview without DB writes
python backfill_velocity.py --session-id <uuid>  # single session
```

### Session name conventions (Catapult)
| Type | Name pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Practice | standalone `P` token | `SP25 - P1 - 03.22.25`, `AUBURN - P3 - 08.26.25` |
| Walk-thru | contains `Walk Thru` | `SP25 - Walk Thru #1 - 03.24.25` |
| Game | standalone `G` token | `AUBURN - G1 - 08.29.25` |
| Mock game | contains `Mock Game` → day type `scrimmage` (kept out of practice norms and practice SPC history) | `FC26 - MOCK GAME - 08.29.26` |

### Install dependencies (first time only, macOS)
```
cd gps_report
~/.local/bin/uv venv .venv --python 3.14
~/.local/bin/uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-dev.txt
```
Never `pip install` globally (Python is PEP 668-managed on this Mac). `pull.sh` and launchd use `gps_report/.venv/bin/python`.

### Regular pull (added 2026-09-13)
- **Owner:** the Mac owns `data/gps_history.duckdb`. The Windows `Refresh_All_Data` GPS step must stay off (two writers = two drifting DBs).
- **Schedule:** `ops/com.keystone.gpspull.plist` → `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, daily 06:30; launchd runs a missed job on wake from sleep, not after power-off. Logs: `gps_report/logs/launchd-gpspull.{log,err}`.
- **Receipt:** every `bulk_import.py` run writes `logs/last_run.json` (status, exit code, window, counts, `imported_dates`, `last_success_at`). Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 usage/config/token · 2 DB open/lock · 3 partial · 4 all listing windows failed or roster fetch failed · 5 unexpected.
- **Alerts:** `pull.sh` appends one line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at Claude Code session start) on a non-zero import, a failed snapshot export, or no successful pull for 36 h.
- **Atomic sessions:** a session's header and athlete rows commit together or not at all; any stats row without an athlete id fails the session so it is retried.
- **Retry backlog:** the receipt's `retry_from` is the earliest date of any failed listing window or unstored session. The next `--since-db` run starts at the earlier of `newest − overlap_days` and `retry_from`, so a later success never strands an earlier failure. Only a clean `--since-db` run clears it; range and dry runs never do.
- Plan and Codex review: `docs/2026-09-13-pull-build-PLAN.md`, `docs/2026-09-13-pull-build-REVIEW-LOG.md`.

### Parquet snapshots for Windows (added 2026-09-24)
The DB never travels. After every ok/partial import, `pull.sh` runs `export_snapshot.py`, which opens the DB
read-only and writes one Parquet file per table to Google Drive. **Only the Mac writes them.** Windows reads
them directly and never writes the DB or the snapshots.
- **Where:** `$ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR/gps/`, else `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/gps/` on Drive
  (Mac `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/...`, Windows `G:\My Drive\...`).
  Files: `athlete_sessions.parquet`, `sessions.parquet`, `athletes.parquet`, `positional_norms.parquet`, plus

import yaml

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Practice-type classifier
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_PRACTICE_RE = re.compile(r'\bP\d+\b')     # "P1", "P11", etc. — standalone P number
_GAME_RE     = re.compile(r'\bG\d+\b')     # "G1", "G12", etc. — standalone G number
_WALKTHRU_RE = re.compile(r'Walk\s*Thru', re.IGNORECASE)
_SCRIMMAGE_RE = re.compile(r'mock\s*game|scrimmage', re.IGNORECASE)  # game-like, kept out of practice norms


def classify_practice_type(session_name: str) -> str:
    """Return 'walkthru', 'scrimmage', 'game', or 'practice' based on session name."""
    if _WALKTHRU_RE.search(session_name):
        return "walkthru"
    if _SCRIMMAGE_RE.search(session_name):
        return "scrimmage"
    if _GAME_RE.search(session_name):
        return "game"
    if _PRACTICE_RE.search(session_name):
        return "practice"
    return "practice"  # default — treat unknown as practice

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Purpose

Athletic performance data infrastructure for Baylor University. The primary active project is an automated post-practice GPS report for Football using the Catapult API. ForceDecks integration is a separate, future project.

## Archived: `archive/coach_report/` (2026-10-19)

The post-session coach report (planned vs actual, max velocity, SPC flags) is **parked**: Eric is not moving forward with it. Code, tests, config and past reports (`archive/coach_report/Reports/coach/`) are kept as-is. `pull.sh` no longer builds it. To revive: move it back to `coach_report/` and restore the coach step in `gps_report/pull.sh` from git history (commit before 2026-10-19). Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-coach-report-design.md`.

## Active Project: `gps_report/`

**Automated post-practice GPS report** — pulls Football session data from Catapult Connect v6 API, stores summary stats in DuckDB, and generates a self-contained HTML report + plain-text email summary.

### Entry points
```
cd gps_report

# Daily report (after practice)
python run_report.py                          # interactive — picks today's session
python run_report.py --date 2026-03-10        # specific date
python run_report.py --session-id <uuid>      # skip picker
python run_report.py --list-positions         # print Catapult position strings (setup)
python run_report.py --force                  # re-import existing session

# Regular pull — the one command (also runs daily at 06:30 via launchd com.keystone.gpspull)
./pull.sh                                     # import new sessions (--since-db), then Parquet snapshots

# Bulk import
python bulk_import.py --since-db              # newest stored date − pull.overlap_days (3) → today
python bulk_import.py                         # 2025-03-22 → today (practices, walk-thrus, games, mock games)
python bulk_import.py --dry-run               # preview matching sessions without DB writes
python bulk_import.py --start 2025-08-01 --end 2025-12-31
python bulk_import.py --force                 # re-import sessions already in DB

# Tests (no network, no real DB)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q

# Backfill / recompute velocity + band columns for historical sessions
python backfill_velocity.py                   # all non-walk-through sessions
python backfill_velocity.py --dry-run         # preview without DB writes
python backfill_velocity.py --session-id <uuid>  # single session
```

### Session name conventions (Catapult)
| Type | Name pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Practice | standalone `P` token | `SP25 - P1 - 03.22.25`, `AUBURN - P3 - 08.26.25` |
| Walk-thru | contains `Walk Thru` | `SP25 - Walk Thru #1 - 03.24.25` |
| Game | standalone `G` token | `AUBURN - G1 - 08.29.25` |
| Mock game | contains `Mock Game` → day type `scrimmage` (kept out of practice norms and practice SPC history) | `FC26 - MOCK GAME - 08.29.26` |

### Install dependencies (first time only, macOS)
```
cd gps_report
~/.local/bin/uv venv .venv --python 3.14
~/.local/bin/uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-dev.txt
```
Never `pip install` globally (Python is PEP 668-managed on this Mac). `pull.sh` and launchd use `gps_report/.venv/bin/python`.

### Regular pull (added 2026-09-13)
- **Owner:** the Mac owns `data/gps_history.duckdb`. The Windows `Refresh_All_Data` GPS step must stay off (two writers = two drifting DBs).
- **Schedule:** `ops/com.keystone.gpspull.plist` → `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, daily 06:30; launchd runs a missed job on wake from sleep, not after power-off. Logs: `gps_report/logs/launchd-gpspull.{log,err}`.
- **Receipt:** every `bulk_import.py` run writes `logs/last_run.json` (status, exit code, window, counts, `imported_dates`, `last_success_at`). Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 usage/config/token · 2 DB open/lock · 3 partial · 4 all listing windows failed or roster fetch failed · 5 unexpected.
- **Alerts:** `pull.sh` appends one line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at Claude Code session start) on a non-zero import, a failed snapshot export, or no successful pull for 36 h.
- **Atomic sessions:** a session's header and athlete rows commit together or not at all; any stats row without an athlete id fails the session so it is retried.
- **Retry backlog:** the receipt's `retry_from` is the earliest date of any failed listing window or unstored session. The next `--since-db` run starts at the earlier of `newest − overlap_days` and `retry_from`, so a later success never strands an earlier failure. Only a clean `--since-db` run clears it; range and dry runs never do.
- Plan and Codex review: `docs/2026-09-13-pull-build-PLAN.md`, `docs/2026-09-13-pull-build-REVIEW-LOG.md`.

### Parquet snapshots for Windows (added 2026-09-24)
The DB never travels. After every ok/partial import, `pull.sh` runs `export_snapshot.py`, which opens the DB
read-only and writes one Parquet file per table to Google Drive. **Only the Mac writes them.** Windows reads
them directly and never writes the DB or the snapshots.
- **Where:** `$ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR/gps/`, else `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/gps/` on Drive
  (Mac `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/...`, Windows `G:\My Drive\...`).
  Files: `athlete_sessions.parquet`, `sessions.parquet`, `athletes.parquet`, `positional_norms.parquet`, plus
  `manifest.json` (per table: rows, bytes, written_at UTC, machine, newest `session_date`). No table is skipped
  (the DB has no log tables); `_`-prefixed work tables would be.
- **Read on Windows:** `duckdb.sql("select * from 'G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/gps/athlete_sessions.parquet'")`.
- **Atomic:** each file is written as `<table>.parquet.tmp` and renamed, so Drive never syncs half a file.
- **Stale-writer guard:** a table whose snapshot already records MORE rows than this DB is refused (exit 3,
  the others are still written) unless `--force`. It stops a stale copy of the DB clobbering the Mac's
  snapshot. `positional_norms` is rebuilt by `compute_norms.py`, so after a rebuild that shrinks it, run
  `export_snapshot.py --force` by hand.
- **Failure:** export exit codes 0 ok · 1 error · 2 no DB / Drive not mounted · 3 refused. A non-zero export
  appends `snapshot-export exit=N` to the alert log and is recorded in `logs/last_run.json` under
  `snapshot_export`; the pull's own exit code is unchanged.
- **By hand (Mac):** `cd gps_report && .venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run`.

### Key files
- [gps_report/run_report.py](gps_report/run_report.py) — entry point; session picker, data fetch, report render
- [gps_report/bulk_import.py](gps_report/bulk_import.py) — bulk historical import (practices, walk-thrus, games)
- [gps_report/config.yaml](gps_report/config.yaml) — flagging thresholds, position groups, region
- [gps_report/.env](gps_report/.env) — `CATAPULT_TOKEN=<jwt>` (not in git)
- [gps_report/src/api_client.py](gps_report/src/api_client.py) — Catapult Connect v6 REST client
- [gps_report/src/storage.py](gps_report/src/storage.py) — DuckDB schema + queries
- [gps_report/src/baseline.py](gps_report/src/baseline.py) — rolling 28-day baseline + flagging
- [gps_report/src/report_builder.py](gps_report/src/report_builder.py) — HTML + email text generation
- [gps_report/templates/report.html.j2](gps_report/templates/report.html.j2) — Jinja2 report template
- [gps_report/backfill_velocity.py](gps_report/backfill_velocity.py) — re-fetch and recompute velocity + band columns for historical sessions

### Architecture
```
POST /stats (Catapult Connect v6)
  └── api_client.py  →  storage.py (DuckDB)
                              └── baseline.py  →  report_builder.py  →  Reports/YYYY-MM-DD/
```

### API details (Catapult Connect v6)
- **Base URL:** `https://connect-us.catapultsports.com/api/v6`
- **Auth:** JWT Bearer token in `gps_report/.env` as `CATAPULT_TOKEN`
- **Token scope:** `connect`, `catapultr`, `sensor-read-only`
- **Activities filter:** `start_time` / `end_time` are **Unix timestamps** (not ISO 8601)
- **Stats endpoint:** `POST /stats` with `filters: [{name: "activity_id", comparison: "=", values: [uuid]}]`
- **Stats source:** `cached_stats`, `group_by: ["athlete"]`
- **`POST /stats` works** and returns 200 — `bake_status=unprocessed` does NOT block it
- **Do NOT use:** `maximum_velocity`, `high_speed_running_distance`, `athlete_max_velocity`, `percentage_max_velocity`, `deceleration_density` — return 0 or wrong slugs for this account
- **`max_vel`** = session max velocity in **mph** — multiply × 0.44704 to store as m/s
- **`velocity_band3_total_distance`** = HSD (75–90% of max vel), in meters
- **`velocity_band4–8_total_distance`** = sprint bands; bands 5–8 always return 0 for Baylor
- **Full parameter list** available at `GET /parameters` — 1,829 slugs. Saved to `logs/all_parameters.json`.

### Metric field mapping (API → DB)
| API field | DB column | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `average_player_load` | `total_player_load` | session average per athlete, not cumulative |
| `total_distance` | `total_distance_m` | stored in meters; displayed in yards |
| `max_vel` | `max_velocity_ms` | API value is mph; stored m/s (`× 0.44704`); displayed mph |
| `velocity_band3_total_distance` | `vb3_distance_m` + `high_speed_distance_m` | raw band stored; derived metric computed from config |
| `velocity_band4–8_total_distance` | `vb4–vb8_distance_m` + `sprint_distance_m` | raw bands stored; derived metric summed from config |
| `velocity_band3/4_total_effort_count` | `vb3_effort_count`, `vb4_effort_count` | # entries into HSD/sprint zones |
| `acceleration_density` | `accel_density` | |
| `explosive_efforts` | `explosive_efforts` | = `total_high_ima` (same values) |
| `total_duration` | `total_duration_s` | session duration in seconds |
| `total_acceleration_load` | `total_accel_load` | |
| `average_velocity` | `average_velocity_ms` | stored m/s |
| `meterage_per_minute` | `meterage_per_minute` | |
| `player_load_per_minute` | `player_load_per_minute` | |
| `explosive_ratio_(avg)` | `explosive_ratio_avg` | |
| `ima_band3_accel/decel/right/left_count` | `ima_high_accel/decel/right/left` | high-intensity IMA counts |
| `high_ima_accel/decel` | `ima_high_accel_decel` | combined high IMA accel+decel |
| `total_high/medium/low_ima(_movements)` | `total_high/medium/low_ima` | IMA movement tier totals |
| `ima/min`, `total_high_ima/min`, `total_high_ima_(avg)` | `ima_per_minute`, `total_high_ima_per_min`, `total_high_ima_avg` | IMA rate/avg metrics |
| `impacts_low/med/high` | `impacts_low/med/high` | collision/contact event counts |
| `impact_low_(avg)`, `impacts_med_(avg)`, `impacts_high_(avg)` | `impacts_low/med/high_avg` | impact averages |
| `pl_low/med/high/veryhigh` | `pl_low/med/high/veryhigh` | player load band totals |
| `pl_med_(avg)` | `pl_high_avg` | ⚠️ Catapult name/slug mismatch — slug says "med" but value is PL_High (Avg) |
| `pl_veryhigh_(avg)`, `pl_veryhigh/min` | `pl_veryhigh_avg`, `pl_veryhigh_per_min` | |
| `total_lineman_contact_count` | `total_contacts` | all players (not just linemen despite name) |
| `total_qb_throw_count` | `total_throws` | QB-specific; zero for all non-QB athletes |

### Velocity band storage architecture
Raw band columns (`vb3_distance_m`–`vb8_distance_m`) are stored as DB ground truth. Derived metrics (`high_speed_distance_m`, `sprint_distance_m`) are computed at ingest from `config.yaml` `metrics.derived` band assignments — same principle as m→yds/m/s→mph unit conversions. To redefine HSD or Sprint zones: edit `config.yaml` → run `python backfill_velocity.py`. No code changes needed.

### Athlete roster API fields (`GET /athletes`)
- **Name:** `first_name` + `last_name` (separate fields — no `full_name`, `name`, or `displayName`)
- **Jersey:** `jersey` field (string, may be non-numeric e.g. `"DBB"`) — parse to `int`, store `NULL` if non-numeric
- **Position:** `position_name` (e.g. `"DL"`) preferred over `position` (single-letter code e.g. `"D"`)
- Parsed in `parse_athlete()` in both `run_report.py` and `bulk_import.py`

### Position group mapping
Run `--list-positions` to see actual Catapult position strings. Config already updated with live values from web UI. Position names from `GET /athletes` include `position_name` field.

### HTML report layout (sections, top to bottom)
1. Header band (Baylor green) — wordmark, session name/date, athlete count
2. Gold accent bar
3. KPI tiles (4) — Team Avg PL · Avg Distance (yds) · Avg Max Speed mph (N/A when 0) · Avg Explosive Efforts
4. Charts row — SVG volume trend sparkline (last 10 sessions) + Top Speeds CSS bars (top 8 by mph)
5. Position Group Summary table — group, N, avg PL, avg dist (yds), avg speed (mph), avg HSD (yds), avg explosive; high/low cell shading
6. Athlete Flags — card layout per athlete, HIGH (orange) / LOW (blue) badges with baseline context
7. Offensive Breakdown — Skill, OL group player tables
8. Defensive Breakdown — DBs, STAR, LB, DL group player tables
9. Other — Special Teams
10. Footer

### Display units
- **Distance:** stored in meters (DB), displayed in **yards** everywhere in report (`m_to_yds()` in `src/utils.py`)
- **Velocity:** stored in m/s (DB), displayed in **mph** everywhere in report (`ms_to_mph()` in `src/utils.py`)
- Do NOT change DB storage units — conversion is display-layer only

### Baseline flagging
- Activates after 3 sessions per athlete (configurable: `flagging.min_sessions_for_baseline`)
- Default: flag if value is >1.5 SD from rolling 28-day personal average
- Metrics flagged: Total Player Load, Total Distance, High Speed Distance

### Jinja2 + pandas NA gotcha
Pandas `NA` values (from DuckDB nullable integer columns like `jersey_number`) cannot be evaluated as booleans in Jinja2 (`{% if athlete.jersey_number %}`). Always convert with `None if pd.isna(val) else val` in `report_builder.py` before passing to the template.

### DuckDB lock risk
`data/gps_history.duckdb` allows one writer. A second writer (a manual `run_report.py` or import during the 06:30 pull) fails fast with a lock error — the import exits 2 and alerts. Never put the DB in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive / OneDrive sync locks it); it stays local and gitignored.

## Architecture Decisions

- **Scope:** Football GPS only — ForceDecks is a separate future project
- **Storage:** DuckDB local file (`gps_report/data/gps_history.duckdb`) — summary stats only, no raw 10Hz data
- **API:** Catapult Connect v6 (US region); JWT token in `gps_report/.env`
- **Scheduled pull (changed 2026-09-13, Eric):** one local launchd job at 06:30 plus the same `pull.sh` by hand after practice. Replaces "no scheduler — run manually". Still no web server and no auto-email.
- **Files:** Google Drive only (`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/02_SPORTS/Football/FA2026/`) for raw exports; OneDrive is no longer used.

## Technical Environment

- **OS:** macOS (MacBook, since 2026-08-05) owns the DB and the pull. The Windows laptop is still active but does not write GPS data.
- **Python:** 3.14 in `gps_report/.venv` (uv)
- **Languages:** Python (primary), R (available)
- **Visualization:** Self-contained HTML report (active); Power BI (future/optional)
- **Constraint:** Baylor IT approval required for cloud-hosted solutions

## Design Constraints

- Nothing that requires significant effort to fix mid-season if it breaks
- Keep the pipeline transparent and editable without specialized infrastructure knowledge
- Do not propose ForceDecks or Power BI integration in this project — those are separate

Derived metrics (`high_speed_distance_m`, `sprint_distance_m`) are computed at ingest from `config.yaml` `metrics.derived` band assignments — same principle as m→yds/m/s→mph unit conversions. To redefine HSD or Sprint zones: edit `config.yaml` → run `python backfill_velocity.py`. No code changes needed.

### Athlete roster API fields (`GET /athletes`)
- **Name:** `first_name` + `last_name` (separate fields — no `full_name`, `name`, or `displayName`)
- **Jersey:** `jersey` field (string, may be non-numeric e.g. `"DBB"`) — parse to `int`, store `NULL` if non-numeric
- **Position:** `position_name` (e.g. `"DL"`) preferred over `position` (single-letter code e.g. `"D"`)
- Parsed in `parse_athlete()` in both `run_report.py` and `bulk_import.py`

### Position group mapping
Run `--list-positions` to see actual Catapult position strings. Config already updated with live values from web UI. Position names from `GET /athletes` include `position_name` field.

### HTML report layout (sections, top to bottom)
1. Header band (Baylor green) — wordmark, session name/date, athlete count
2. Gold accent bar
3. KPI tiles (4) — Team Avg PL · Avg Distance (yds) · Avg Max Speed mph (N/A when 0) · Avg Explosive Efforts
4. Charts row — SVG volume trend sparkline (last 10 sessions) + Top Speeds CSS bars (top 8 by mph)
5. Position Group Summary table — group, N, avg PL, avg dist (yds), avg speed (mph), avg HSD (yds), avg explosive; high/low cell shading
6. Athlete Flags — card layout per athlete, HIGH (orange) / LOW (blue) badges with baseline context
7. Offensive Breakdown — Skill, OL group player tables
8. Defensive Breakdown — DBs, STAR, LB, DL group player tables
9. Other — Special Teams
10. Footer

### Display units
- **Distance:** stored in meters (DB), displayed in **yards** everywhere in report (`m_to_yds()` in `src/utils.py`)
- **Velocity:** stored in m/s (DB), displayed in **mph** everywhere in report (`ms_to_mph()` in `src/utils.py`)
- Do NOT change DB storage units — conversion is display-layer only

### Baseline flagging
- Activates after 3 sessions per athlete (configurable: `flagging.min_sessions_for_baseline`)
- Default: flag if value is >1.5 SD from rolling 28-day personal average
- Metrics flagged: Total Player Load, Total Distance, High Speed Distance

### Jinja2 + pandas NA gotcha
Pandas `NA` values (from DuckDB nullable integer columns like `jersey_number`) cannot be evaluated as booleans in Jinja2 (`{% if athlete.jersey_number %}`). Always convert with `None if pd.isna(val) else val` in `report_builder.py` before passing to the template.

### DuckDB lock risk
`data/gps_history.duckdb` allows one writer. A second writer (a manual `run_report.py` or import during the 06:30 pull) fails fast with a lock error — the import exits 2 and alerts. Never put the DB in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive / OneDrive sync locks it); it stays local and gitignored.

## Architecture Decisions

- **Scope:** Football GPS only — ForceDecks is a separate future project
- **Storage:** DuckDB local file (`gps_report/data/gps_history.duckdb`) — summary stats only, no raw 10Hz data
- **API:** Catapult Connect v6 (US region); JWT token in `gps_report/.env`
- **Scheduled pull (changed 2026-09-13, Eric):** one local launchd job at 06:30 plus the same `pull.sh` by hand after practice. Replaces "no scheduler — run manually". Still no web server and no auto-email.
- **Files:** Google Drive only (`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/02_SPORTS/Football/FA2026/`) for raw exports; OneDrive is no longer used.

## Technical Environment

- **OS:** macOS (MacBook, since 2026-08-05) owns the DB and the pull. The Windows laptop is still active but does not write GPS data.
- **Python:** 3.14 in `gps_report/.venv` (uv)
- **Languages:** Python (primary), R (available)
- **Visualization:** Self-contained HTML report (active); Power BI (future/optional)
- **Constraint:** Baylor IT approval required for cloud-hosted solutions

## Design Constraints

- Nothing that requires significant effort to fix mid-season if it breaks
- Keep the pipeline transparent and editable without specialized infrastructure knowledge
- Do not propose ForceDecks or Power BI integration in this project — those are separate

"""Pull Catapult PlayerLoad band durations per athlete per session (2025 + 2026 fall).

Read-only on gps_history.duckdb (session list, names, positions). Never writes the DB or
touches the daily pull. Calls the catapult-openfield-connect-pp-cli once per session and
caches the JSON, so re-runs only fetch new sessions.

    gps_report/.venv/bin/python analysis/pl_bands/pull_pl_bands.py           # fetch + build
    gps_report/.venv/bin/python analysis/pl_bands/pull_pl_bands.py --refetch-since 2026-10-25

Output: gps_report/data/pl_bands/pl_bands.parquet (gitignored; athlete names inside).
Band edges (all athletes, unchanged since 2022-10-04): B1 0-0.7, B2 0.7-1.5, B3 1.5-2,
B4 2-2.5, B5 2.5-3, B6 3-3.5, B7 3.5-4, B8 4+.
"""
import argparse, json, subprocess, sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
GPS = ROOT / "gps_report"
sys.path.insert(0, str(GPS))
from compute_norms import classify_practice_type  # noqa: E402  (same rule as the norms)

DB = GPS / "data" / "gps_history.duckdb"
OUT = GPS / "data" / "pl_bands"
CACHE = OUT / "cache"
CLI = Path.home() / ".local/bin/catapult-openfield-connect-pp-cli"
# shortcut: fall seasons only (Jul 20 - Dec 31); widen if spring/summer is needed.
SEASONS = [("2025-07-20", "2025-12-31"), ("2026-07-20", "2026-12-31")]
PARAMS = [f"player_load_band{i}_total_duration" for i in range(1, 9)] + [
    "total_duration", "total_player_load", "player_load_per_minute"]


def fetch(session_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    flt = json.dumps([{"name": "activity_id", "comparison": "=", "values": [session_id]}])
    r = subprocess.run([str(CLI), "stats", "--parameters", ",".join(PARAMS), "--group-by", "athlete",
                        "--requested-only=false", "--filters", flt, "--json", "--data-source", "live"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{session_id}: exit {r.returncode}: {r.stderr[:300]}")
    return json.loads(r.stdout)["results"]


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--refetch-since", help="re-pull cached sessions on/after this date (Catapult reprocessing)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
    where = " or ".join(f"(session_date between '{s}' and '{e}')" for s, e in SEASONS)
    sessions = con.execute(f"select session_id, session_name, session_date from sessions where {where} "
                           "order by session_date").df()
    athletes = con.execute("select catapult_id as athlete_id, position, position_group from athletes").df()
    con.close()

    failed = []
    for s in sessions.itertuples():
        f = CACHE / f"{s.session_id}.json"
        stale = a.refetch_since and str(s.session_date) >= a.refetch_since
        if f.exists() and not stale:
            continue
        try:
            f.write_text(json.dumps(fetch(s.session_id)))
            print("fetched", s.session_date, s.session_name)
        except Exception as e:  # keep going; report at the end
            failed.append(str(e)); print("FAILED", e, file=sys.stderr)

    rows = []
    for s in sessions.itertuples():
        f = CACHE / f"{s.session_id}.json"
        if not f.exists():
            continue
        for r in json.loads(f.read_text()):
            rows.append({"session_id": s.session_id, "session_name": s.session_name,
                         "session_date": s.session_date, "athlete_id": r.get("athlete_id"),
                         "athlete_name": r.get("athlete_name"), **{p: r.get(p) for p in PARAMS}})
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).merge(athletes, on="athlete_id", how="left")
    df["day_type"] = df["session_name"].map(classify_practice_type)
    df["season"] = pd.to_datetime(df["session_date"]).dt.year
    band_sum = df[[f"player_load_band{i}_total_duration" for i in range(1, 9)]].sum(axis=1)
    df["band_gap_s"] = df["total_duration"] - band_sum
    # Rows with no time on the unit (device off/not worn) carry no information.
    df = df[df["total_duration"].fillna(0) > 0]
    bad = (df["band_gap_s"].abs() > 0.02 * df["total_duration"]).sum()
    assert bad <= 0.01 * len(df), f"{bad} rows where bands do not add up to total_duration"
    df.to_parquet(OUT / "pl_bands.parquet", index=False)
    print(f"{len(df)} athlete-sessions, {df.session_id.nunique()} sessions; band-sum mismatches: {bad}; "
          f"failed fetches: {len(failed)}")
    if failed:
        sys.exit(3)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Pull Catapult PlayerLoad band durations per athlete per session (2025 + 2026 fall).

Read-only on gps_history.duckdb (session list, names, positions). Never writes the DB or
touches the daily pull. Calls the catapult-openfield-connect-pp-cli once per session and
caches the JSON, so re-runs only fetch new sessions.

    gps_report/.venv/bin/python analysis/pl_bands/pull_pl_bands.py           # fetch + build
    gps_report/.venv/bin/python analysis/pl_bands/pull_pl_bands.py --refetch-since 2026-10-25

Output: gps_report/data/pl_bands/pl_bands.parquet (gitignored; athlete names inside).
Band edges (all athletes, unchanged since 2022-10-04): B1 0-0.7, B2 0.7-1.5, B3 1.5-2,
B4 2-2.5, B5 2.5-3, B6 3-3.5, B7 3.5-4, B8 4+.
"""
import argparse, json, subprocess, sys
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
GPS = ROOT / "gps_report"
sys.path.insert(0, str(GPS))
from compute_norms import classify_practice_type  # noqa: E402  (same rule as the norms)

DB = GPS / "data" / "gps_history.duckdb"
OUT = GPS / "data" / "pl_bands"
CACHE = OUT / "cache"
CLI = Path.home() / ".local/bin/catapult-openfield-connect-pp-cli"
# shortcut: fall seasons only (Jul 20 - Dec 31); widen if spring/summer is needed.
SEASONS = [("2025-07-20", "2025-12-31"), ("2026-07-20", "2026-12-31")]
PARAMS = [f"player_load_band{i}_total_duration" for i in range(1, 9)] + [
    "total_duration", "total_player_load", "player_load_per_minute"]


def fetch(session_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    flt = json.dumps([{"name": "activity_id", "comparison": "=", "values": [session_id]}])
    r = subprocess.run([str(CLI), "stats", "--parameters", ",".join(PARAMS), "--group-by", "athlete",
                        "--requested-only=false", "--filters", flt, "--json", "--data-source", "live"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{session_id}: exit {r.returncode}: {r.stderr[:300]}")
    return json.loads(r.stdout)["results"]


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--refetch-since", help="re-pull cached sessions on/after this date (Catapult reprocessing)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
    where = " or ".join(f"(session_date between '{s}' and '{e}')" for s, e in SEASONS)
    sessions = con.execute(f"select session_id, session_name, session_date from sessions where {where} "
                           "order by session_date").df()
    athletes = con.execute("select catapult_id as athlete_id, position, position_group from athletes").df()
    con.close()

    failed = []
    for s in sessions.itertuples():
        f = CACHE / f"{s.session_id}.json"
        stale = a.refetch_since and str(s.session_date) >= a.refetch_since
        if f.exists() and not stale:
            continue
        try:
            f.write_text(json.dumps(fetch(s.session_id)))
            print("fetched", s.session_date, s.session_name)
        except Exception as e:  # keep going; report at the end
            failed.append(str(e)); print("FAILED", e, file=sys.stderr)

    rows = []
    for s in sessions.itertuples():
        f = CACHE / f"{s.session_id}.json"
        if not f.exists():
            continue
        for r in json.loads(f.read_text()):
            rows.append({"session_id": s.session_id, "session_name": s.session_name,
                         "session_date": s.session_date, "athlete_id": r.get("athlete_id"),
                         "athlete_name": r.get("athlete_name"), **{p: r.get(p) for p in PARAMS}})
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).merge(athletes, on="athlete_id", how="left")
    df["day_type"] = df["session_name"].map(classify_practice_type)
    df["season"] = pd.to_datetime(df["session_date"]).dt.year
    band_sum = df[[f"player_load_band{i}_total_duration" for i in range(1, 9)]].sum(axis=1)
    df["band_gap_s"] = df["total_duration"] - band_sum
    # Rows with no time on the unit (device off/not worn) carry no information.
    df = df[df["total_duration"].fillna(0) > 0]
    bad = (df["band_gap_s"].abs() > 0.02 * df["total_duration"]).sum()
    assert bad <= 0.01 * len(df), f"{bad} rows where bands do not add up to total_duration"
    df.to_parquet(OUT / "pl_bands.parquet", index=False)
    print(f"{len(df)} athlete-sessions, {df.session_id.nunique()} sessions; band-sum mismatches: {bad}; "
          f"failed fetches: {len(failed)}")
    if failed:
        sys.exit(3)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Weekly physicality view from PlayerLoad band time (run pull_pl_bands.py first).

    gps_report/.venv/bin/python analysis/pl_bands/weekly_view.py

Metric: B4+ = seconds above PlayerLoad band-4 edge (2.0), per 60 min on the unit.
Why B4+: walk-thrus sit near 0 (3.5 s/h) while practices run ~37 s/h, so it splits
full-speed work from teaching tempo, and it is big enough (60-70 s/session) to be stable.
B6+ (edge 3.0) is the "game-level" tail: the only level where games beat practice.
Weeks run from the day after one game through the next game; week 1 = all of camp.
"""
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
import pandas as pd

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "gps_report" / "data" / "pl_bands"
pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)


def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    d = duckdb.sql(f"select * from '{OUT / 'pl_bands.parquet'}'").df()
    b = {f"player_load_band{i}_total_duration": f"B{i}" for i in range(1, 9)}
    d = d.rename(columns=b)
    d["B4+"] = d[[f"B{i}" for i in range(4, 9)]].sum(axis=1)
    d["B6+"] = d[[f"B{i}" for i in range(6, 9)]].sum(axis=1)
    d["min"] = d["band_time_s"] / 60
    d["B4ph"] = d["B4+"] / d["min"] * 60
    d["session_date"] = pd.to_datetime(d["session_date"])

    s = d[["session_id", "session_name", "session_date", "day_type", "season"]].drop_duplicates()
    s = s.sort_values("session_date")
    games = s[s.day_type == "game"].copy()
    games["wk_no"] = games.groupby("season").cumcount() + 1
    games["week"] = games.session_name.str.split(" - ").str[:2].str.join(" ")
    # Each session belongs to the next game on/after its date in the same season.
    s = pd.merge_asof(s, games[["session_date", "season", "wk_no", "week"]].rename(
        columns={"session_date": "game_date"}), left_on="session_date", right_on="game_date",
        by="season", direction="forward")
    s["days_to_game"] = (s.game_date - s.session_date).dt.days
    return d.merge(s[["session_id", "wk_no", "week", "days_to_game"]], on="session_id")


def main() -> None:
    d = load()
    p = d[(d.day_type == "practice") & d.wk_no.notna()]
    a = p.groupby(["season", "wk_no", "week", "athlete_id"]).agg(
        B4=("B4+", "sum"), B6=("B6+", "sum"), mins=("min", "sum"),
        n=("session_id", "nunique")).reset_index()
    w = a.groupby(["season", "wk_no", "week"]).agg(
        practices=("n", "max"), minutes=("mins", "median"),
        B4_s=("B4", "median"), B6_s=("B6", "median")).reset_index()
    w["B4+_per_hr"] = w.B4_s / w.minutes * 60
    print("1) PRACTICE WEEKS: median athlete, practice days only")
    print(w.round(1).to_string(index=False))

    q = d[d.day_type.isin(["practice", "walkthru"]) & (d.wk_no > 1)]
    t = q.groupby(["season", "days_to_game"]).agg(B4ph=("B4ph", "median"), mins=("min", "median"),
                                                  n=("session_id", "nunique")).round(1)
    print("\n2) B4+ sec/hr by days before game (weeks 2+)")
    print(t.unstack(0).to_string())

    latest = d[d.season == d.season.max()].wk_no.max()
    last = d[(d.season == d.season.max()) & (d.wk_no == latest)]
    print(f"\n3) LATEST WEEK ({last.week.iloc[0]}), by day")
    print(last.groupby(["session_name", "days_to_game"]).agg(
        B4ph=("B4ph", "median"), B4=("B4+", "median"), B6=("B6+", "median"),
        mins=("min", "median")).round(1).sort_values("days_to_game", ascending=False).to_string())

    pp = d[(d.day_type == "practice") & (d.wk_no > 1)].copy()
    cur = d.season.max()
    pp["bucket"] = pp.apply(lambda r: "latest wk" if (r.season == cur and r.wk_no == latest)
                            else f"{r.season} season", axis=1)
    print("\n4) PRACTICE B4+ sec/hr by position group (weeks 2+)")
    print(pp.groupby(["position_group", "bucket"]).B4ph.median().round(1).unstack().to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# PlayerLoad band time: physicality tracking (started 2026-11-01)

Goal: practice length stays about the same during the taper, but physicality should drop.
Track **time spent above a PlayerLoad band edge**, the way you track heart rate band time.

## Run it (after each week)
```
cd ~/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting
gps_report/.venv/bin/python analysis/pl_bands/pull_pl_bands.py   # fetch new sessions only (cached)
gps_report/.venv/bin/python analysis/pl_bands/weekly_view.py     # print the 4 tables
```
Reads the session list from `gps_history.duckdb` read-only, so run `pull.sh` first if a session is new.
Output: `gps_report/data/pl_bands/pl_bands.parquet` (gitignored). It never writes the DB.
